facts.fact: Kanazawa Umimirai Library is a public library in Kanazawa, Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan.
facts.quote: Kanazawa Umimirai Library is a public library located in Kanazawa city, Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan.

facts.fact: It is a contemporary building by Kazumi Kudo and Hiroshi Horiba, completed in 2011.
facts.quote: This is a contemporary building by the Japanese architects Kazumi Kudo and Hiroshi Horiba, completed in 2011.

facts.fact: Some 6,000 small circular glass blocks puncture the concrete surface in a triangular array, making a decorative grid.
facts.quote: Its surface creates a decorative grid made of some 6000 small circular blocks of glass which puncture the concrete surface of the building in a triangular array.

facts.fact: The designers, Coelacanth K&H, describe it as a simple space 45 m by 45 m and 12 m high.
facts.quote: The firm that designed the library, Coelacanth K&H, describe the building as a "simple space" of 45m by 45m and 12m high.

facts.fact: The floor area is 5,641.9 square metres.
facts.quote: The floor area is 5,641.9 square metres; the building's area is 2,311.9 square metres.

facts.fact: The single quiet room is meant to resemble a forest, filled with soft light and a feeling of openness.
facts.quote: The "single quiet and tranquil room ... resembles a forest, filled with soft light and a feeling of openness reminiscent of the outdoors".

facts.fact: Horiba and Kudo won a Japan Institute of Architects Prize for the library in 2013.
facts.quote: Hiroshi Horiba and Kazumi Kudo won a Japan Institute of Architects Prize for the library in 2013.

facts.fact: Also known as the Haruki Murakami Library, it is an academic building, library and exhibition space at Waseda University, designed by Kengo Kuma.
facts.quote: The Waseda International House of Literature, also known as the Haruki Murakami Library, is an academic building, library, and museum exhibition space at Waseda University in Shinjuku designed by Japanese architect Kengo Kuma.

facts.fact: Murakami, a Waseda graduate, donated thousands of books, records and archival materials to the university.
facts.quote: Decades later, Murakami decided to donate thousands of books, vinyls, and archival materials to the university for archival purposes.

facts.fact: The project rebuilt, remodelled and renovated the old Building 4 on the campus, over three years from 2018.
facts.quote: As a "rebuilding, remodeling, and renovation of the old Building 4" on Waseda University's campus, the building's envisioning and subsequent construction took three years, starting in 2018.

facts.fact: Kuma imagined a lively place to discuss Murakami's work over coffee, rather than a formal, hushed study space.
facts.quote: In designing the building, Kuma "envisioned a lively place where anyone, including Murakami himself, could come to discuss the novelist's works and the future of literature over coffee, instead of a formal space for studying and whispering in hushed tones."

facts.fact: It opened to the public on 1 October 2021.
facts.quote: The building debuted for public entry on October 1, 2021.

facts.fact: The library holds over 3,000 of Murakami's novels in various editions and in over 50 languages.
facts.quote: The library portion of the building hosts over 3,000 of Murakami's novels in various editions and translated in over 50 languages.

facts.fact: On the second floor a public listening room lets visitors play records.
facts.quote: On the second floor, the building possesses a public listening room with an audio system where visitors can play records.

facts.fact: It is one of the tallest buildings in Naha and the centre of government functions for Okinawa Prefecture.
facts.quote: The Okinawa Prefecture Government Building (Japanese: 沖縄県庁舎, Hepburn: Okinawakenchōsha) is one of the tallest buildings in Naha City, Okinawa, Japan, and is the center for Japanese governmental functions stretching across Okinawa Prefecture.

facts.fact: It opened in 1990, cost nearly 22 billion yen and was designed by Kisho Kurokawa.
facts.quote: The building opened in 1990 and cost nearly 22 billion yen (about 200 million USD). It was designed by architect Kisho Kurokawa.

facts.fact: It has 14 floors above ground and two below, including a city hall and a government information centre.
facts.quote: There are 14 floors above ground and two below including a city hall and government information center.

facts.fact: The top floor holds an observation deck with a panoramic view of Naha.
facts.quote: The top floor houses an observation deck where a panoramic view of Naha City can be seen.

facts.fact: Yufuin Station is a railway station in Yufu, Ōita Prefecture, operated by JR Kyushu.
facts.quote: Yufuin Station (由布院駅, Yufuin-eki)  is a passenger railway station located in Yufuin neighborhood of the city of Yufu, Ōita Prefecture, Japan, operated by JR Kyushu.

facts.fact: The station building was completed in 1990, designed by Arata Isozaki, an architect from Ōita, and inspired by a chapel.
facts.quote: The station building was completed in 1990. It was designed by Arata Isozaki, an architect from Oita Prefecture, and is inspired by a chapel.

facts.fact: It has a black-painted wooden exterior, a 12-metre-high open concourse in the centre, and a waiting room that doubles as an event hall.
facts.quote: It has a wooden, black-painted exterior, with a 12 meter high open concourse in the center, and an adjacent waiting room that doubles as an event hall.

facts.fact: Large glass doors can close the concourse off from the platform against wind, and the waiting room is floor-heated with hot spring water.
facts.quote: The concourse and platform can be separated by large, thick glass doors to prevent wind, and the waiting room has floor heating equipment that uses hot spring water.

facts.fact: The building houses a Yufuin Onsen tourist information centre.
facts.quote: The station has a Midori no Madoguchi staffed ticket office and there is a Yufuin Onsen tourist information center within the station building.

facts.fact: The station is served by the Kyudai Main Line.
facts.quote: Yufuin Station is served by the Kyudai Main Line and is located 99.1 km from the starting point of the line at Kurume.

facts.fact: Hibiya Public Hall, in Hibiya Park, Tokyo, was Japan's first full-scale concert hall and is a designated Tokyo cultural property.
facts.quote: The Hibiya Public Hall is a public hall located in Hibiya Park, Chiyoda, Tokyo, Japan. It was Japan's first full-scale concert hall and is designated as a Historic Building Selected by Tokyo and a Tokyo Metropolitan Designated Tangible Cultural Property (Structure).

facts.fact: Kōichi Satō designed it after winning first place in a design competition; it was completed on 19 October 1929.
facts.quote: The building was designed by Kōichi Satō, who won first place in a designated design competition, and was completed on October 19, 1929.

facts.fact: It forms one complex with the Shisei Kaikan, with a basement, six floors above ground and a four-storey tower.
facts.quote: It forms a complex building with the Shisei Kaikan (Municipal Research Building), consisting of 1 basement level, 6 above-ground floors, and a 4-story tower.

facts.fact: The entrance is on the park side, with the second floor a balcony joined to the park's gardens.
facts.quote: The entrance to the public hall is on the park side, with the second floor designed as a balcony integrated with the park's gardens.

facts.fact: The exterior is clad in brownish scratch tiles in a Neo-Gothic style.
facts.quote: The exterior is clad in brownish scratch tiles in a Neo-Gothic style.

facts.fact: As one of the early steel-frame reinforced concrete buildings, it matters in the history of architectural engineering.
facts.quote: As one of the early steel-frame reinforced concrete buildings, it is considered historically important in architectural engineering.

facts.fact: After the 1923 Great Kantō earthquake, the ground was reinforced with over 2,000 pine piles.
facts.quote: Lessons from the 1923 Great Kantō earthquake led to the ground being reinforced with over 2,000 pine piles.

facts.fact: Closed since 2016 for seismic renovation, it is expected to reopen in 2029, its centenary.
facts.quote: Due to seismic issues, it has been closed for renovation since 2016. It is expected to reopen in 2029, the 100th anniversary of its opening.

facts.fact: Sacred Heart Cathedral is the seat of the bishop of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Yokohama.
facts.quote: Sacred Heart Cathedral (Japanese: カトリック山手教会) is the seat of the bishop of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Yokohama, Japan.

facts.fact: Because it stands at 44 Yamate-cho, it is known locally as Yamate Catholic Church.
facts.quote: As it is located at 44 Yamate-cho, Naka-ku, the cathedral is commonly known locally as Yamate Catholic Church (カトリック山手教会, Katorikku Yamate Kyōkai).

facts.fact: The first church was built in 1862 by the Paris Foreign Missions Society in Yokohama's foreign settlement, just after a long ban on Christianity was lifted.
facts.quote: Immediately after the lifting of the a long-standing ban on Christianity, a Catholic church was built in 1862 by the Paris Foreign Missions Society in the Yokohama foreign settlement (currently Yamashita-cho).

facts.fact: The earlier church, a brick building with two bell towers moved to this site in 1906, was destroyed in the 1923 Great Kantō earthquake.
facts.quote: This church was moved to its current location in 1906, and was a brick building with two bell towers, which was completely destroyed during the 1923 Great Kantō earthquake.

facts.fact: The rebuilt church was designed by the Czech architect Jan Josef Švagr in the Neo-Gothic style and completed in 1933.
facts.quote: The rebuilt Yamate Catholic Church was designed by Czech architect Jan Josef Švagr in the Neo-Gothic style and completed in 1933.

facts.fact: It became the cathedral when the Diocese of Yokohama was created in 1937.
facts.quote: When the Diocese of Yokohama was erected in 1937, the Yamate church became its cathedral.

facts.fact: Švagr was a Czech architect who worked mainly in Japan, where he moved in 1923.
facts.quote: Jan Josef Švagr (7 September 1885, Týnčany – 26 March 1969, Claypole) was a Czech architect who worked mainly in Japan. He moved to Japan in 1923 and started working there, designing many buildings.

facts.fact: It is the mother church of the Anglican Church of Korea and the Diocese of Seoul, next to Deoksugung and Seoul City Hall.
facts.quote: It is the mother church of both the Anglican Church of Korea and the Diocese of Seoul. Its location is adjacent to Deoksugung, the British Embassy in Seoul, Seoul Metropolitan Council, and Seoul City Hall.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1922 to a design by the English architect Arthur Stansfield Dixon.
facts.quote: Construction began in 1922 to a design by English architect Arthur Stansfield Dixon.

facts.fact: It is known for its Romanesque Revival architecture and its mosaic murals.
facts.quote: The Cathedral is known for its Romanesque Revival architecture, together with its mosaic murals.

facts.fact: In 1926 building stopped for lack of money, with only about half of the original plan complete.
facts.quote: 1926 - Construction came to a halt due to financial difficulties, and only about half of the original construction plan was completed.

facts.fact: The expansion began in 1991 after the lost original blueprints were rediscovered in the British Museum archives, and was completed in 1996.
facts.quote: 1991 - The expansion of the Cathedral began. The Seoul City Government had initially rejected plans for the expansion, but later granted permission after the original blueprints, lost during either World War II or the Korean War, were improbably rediscovered at the British Museum archives.

facts.fact: In 1978 the Seoul Metropolitan Government designated it Tangible Cultural Property No. 35.
facts.quote: In 1978, the Cathedral was designated by the Seoul Metropolitan Government as Tangible Cultural Property No. 35.

facts.fact: Dixon, an English metal worker and architect, founded the Birmingham Guild of Handicraft.
facts.quote: He founded the Birmingham Guild of Handicraft and designed their headquarters in Great Charles Street.

facts.fact: The cathedral was a key historical site of the June 1987 protests.
facts.quote: 1987 - Seoul Anglican Cathedral became a key historical site of the June 10th Protest.

facts.fact: Guangzhou Library is the public library of Guangzhou; its new building in Zhujiang New Town fully opened on 23 June 2013.
facts.quote: Guangzhou Library (Chinese: 广州图书馆) is a public library in Guangzhou, capital of Guangdong province, China. The library has moved to a new building in Zhujiang New Town, which fully opened on 23 June 2013.

facts.fact: Nikken Sekkei lists the Guangzhou Library (2013) among its selected projects.
facts.quote: Guangzhou Library, 2013

facts.fact: The new library sits by the Pearl River on Flower City Square, on the city's new central axis.
facts.quote: The new Guangzhou Library is situated on the banks of the Pearl River on Flower City Square and on Guangzhou's new central axis.

facts.fact: Its design concept is "Beautiful Books", and its placement follows the city's new central axis.
facts.quote: The new library uses "Beautiful Books" as the design concept, and the placement of the structure is based on the city's new central axis.

facts.fact: From east to west, the north and south towers resemble the Chinese character 之.
facts.quote: Taken from east to west, the design of the north and south towers bears a resemblance to the Chinese character "之".

facts.fact: The cascading "books" on the exterior stand for the overlap of history and culture.
facts.quote: The cascading style of the "books" on the exterior is representative of the overlap of history and culture.

facts.fact: The design also takes in the arcade and elements of Lingnan art.
facts.quote: At the same time, the design integrates the typical architectural concept of arcade, and embodies elements of Lingnan art.

facts.fact: The building covers 100,000 square metres and provides 4,000 seats.
facts.quote: The new Guangzhou Library covers a gross area of 100 thousand square meters and holds 8.43 million collection. It provides four thousand seats and 500 computers for readers to use.

facts.fact: Wuhan railway station is one of the three main passenger railway stations of Wuhan, capital of Hubei Province.
facts.quote: Wuhan railway station (武汉站; 武漢站) is one of the three main passenger railway stations of Wuhan, the capital of China's Hubei Province.

facts.fact: It was designed by AREP, the Fourth Survey and Design Institute of China, MaP3 and SNCF-IGOA, after a two-phase competition won in 2005.
facts.quote: The station was designed by AREP (Architecture Recherche Engagement Post-carbone), the Fourth Survey and Design Institute of China, MaP3, and SNCF-IGOA, after winning a two-phase competition in 2005.

facts.fact: The design was inspired by the yellow crane, the symbol of Wuhan.
facts.quote: The design was inspired by the yellow crane, the symbol of Wuhan City.

facts.fact: The roof is meant to resemble the crane's wings and is based on a sine curve.
facts.quote: The distinctive roof is intended to resemble the crane's wings, and is based on a sine curve.

facts.fact: The building has nine separate parts, standing for China's nine provinces, plus a central thoroughfare.
facts.quote: The building consists of nine separated parts, symbolizing China's nine provinces, plus a central thoroughfare.

facts.fact: Construction began in September 2006 and finished in December 2009.
facts.quote: Construction of the station began in September 2006, and was completed in December 2009.

facts.fact: The main arch spans 116 metres and the highest point is 58 metres above the ground.

facts.fact: Completed in December 2009, the station has 11 platforms and 20 tracks.
facts.quote: Completed in December 2009, the station has 11 platforms and 20 tracks.

facts.fact: The HKCEC is one of Hong Kong's two major convention and exhibition venues, in Wan Chai North on Hong Kong Island.
facts.quote: The Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre (HKCEC) is one of the two major convention and exhibition venues in Hong Kong, along with AsiaWorld–Expo. It is located in Wan Chai North, Hong Kong Island.

facts.fact: It was designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill with Wong & Ouyang, with Larry Oltmanns leading the design as SOM's Design Partner.
facts.quote: The venue was designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill LLP, in association with Wong & Ouyang (HK) Ltd. Larry Oltmanns led the design as the Design Partner with SOM.

facts.fact: The original building went up in 1988 on reclaimed land; its glass curtain was the world's largest at the time, looking over the harbour on three sides.
facts.quote: The original building was built on reclaimed land off Gloucester Road in 1988. The glass curtain was the world's largest at the time, overlooking the Victoria Harbour on three sides.

facts.fact: The second phase, on an artificial island, was built from 1994 to 1997 and has a bird-like roof.
facts.quote: The second phase of the centre, located on an artificial island, was constructed from 1994 to 1997, and features a bird-like rooftop (also referred to as a turtle by some critics).

facts.fact: Hotels and apartments were built on top of the complex, which New World Development financed.
facts.quote: The complex's construction was financed by New World Development, with the Renaissance Harbour View Hotel, Grand Hyatt Hong Kong and Harbour View Apartments being built on top of it.

facts.fact: A 2006–2009 expansion brought total exhibition space to nearly 83,000 square metres.
facts.quote: Upon completion, the HK$1.4 billion expansion added 19,400 square metres (209,000 sq ft) to the HKCEC, bringing the total exhibition space to nearly 83,000 square metres (890,000 sq ft) and total rentable function space to over 92,000 square metres (990,000 sq ft).

facts.fact: It was the site of the 1997 Hong Kong handover ceremony.
facts.quote: It also served as the site of the 1997 Hong Kong handover ceremony, which signified the end of British colonial rule.

facts.fact: Hong Kong Central Library is the largest library in Hong Kong and the flagship and headquarters of its public libraries.
facts.quote: Hong Kong Central Library is the largest library in Hong Kong, flagship library of Hong Kong Public Libraries (HKPL) and used as Hong Kong Public Library headquarters, functioning as the territory's National Library.

facts.fact: The 12-storey building faces Victoria Harbour and has a floor area of 33,800 square metres.
facts.quote: Facing Victoria Harbour, the 12-storey high building occupies a gross area of 9,400 square metres (101,000 sq ft) with a floor area of 33,800 square metres (364,000 sq ft).

facts.fact: The arch-shaped doorway on the front facade symbolises the Gate to Knowledge, made of a triangle, square and circle that each carry meaning.
facts.quote: The arch-shaped doorway atop the front facade of the Hong Kong Central Library symbolises the Gate to Knowledge, while the triangle, square and circle which make up the arch all carry further meaning.

facts.fact: The circle stands for the sky, the square for the land and the triangle for the accretion of knowledge.
facts.quote: The circle represents the sky, the square the land and the triangle the accretion of knowledge.

facts.fact: It was designed by the government senior architect Ho Chiu-fan.
facts.quote: The library was designed by government senior architect Ho Chiu-fan.

facts.fact: In 1997 the Provisional Urban Council tied 21–21 between Rocco Yim's design and the original, and the chairman's casting vote kept the original.
facts.quote: On 8 August 1997, the Provisional Urban Council decided to vote between the design by Rocco Yim Sen-kee and the original design, which resulted in a tie with 21 votes each, then Leung, the council's chairman, made the final decision by casting his second vote for the original design, even though Yim's design was praised by architects as much superior to the original.

facts.fact: It opened on 17 May 2001.
facts.quote: Opened on 17 May 2001, the Hong Kong Central Library provides a complete variety of library services including:

facts.fact: It was built as an intelligent building on a network floor, so power and data reach every corner.
facts.quote: Additionally, the library has an intelligent building design. Power and data lines reach every corner of the building, laying the necessary foundation for digital service.

facts.fact: It is an academic building at City University of Hong Kong, completed in 2011.
facts.quote: Run Run Shaw Creative Media Centre is an academic building on the campus of the City University of Hong Kong, which was completed in 2011.

facts.fact: It was designed by Daniel Libeskind with Leigh and Orange, and won several design awards.
facts.quote: It was designed by Daniel Libeskind cooperating with Leigh and Orange Ltd., and received several awards on its design.

facts.fact: It was funded by a HK$100 million donation from the Shaw Foundation and is named after Run Run Shaw.
facts.quote: It was funded with a donation of HK$100 million from the Shaw Foundation and is named after Run Run Shaw.

facts.fact: It houses the School of Creative Media and the computer science, media and communication, and English departments.
facts.quote: The building houses the university's School of Creative Media, the Centre for Applied Computing and Interactive Media and the computer science, media and communication, and English departments.

facts.fact: Libeskind's work on it ran from 2002 to 2011.

facts.fact: The critic William J. R. Curtis, in Architectural Review, called it "a pile-up of Libeskindian clichés without sense, form or meaning".
facts.quote: William JR Curtis in Architectural Review called his Run Run Shaw Creative Media Centre "a pile-up of Libeskindian clichés without sense, form or meaning" and wrote that his Hyundai Development Corporation Headquarters delivered "a trite and noisy corporate message".

facts.fact: Completed in 2007 for the China Poly Group, the complex holds the company headquarters, offices, shops, restaurants and the Poly Museum.
facts.quote: Completed in 2007 for the China Poly Group Corporation, it houses the company headquarters, other office space, retail, restaurants, and the Poly Museum.

facts.fact: It was designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM).
facts.quote: The Poly Corporation Headquarters in Beijing, designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM), serves as a central hub for the company's subsidiaries.

facts.fact: It has three parts: an L-shaped office building, a 21-storey glass atrium and a hanging structure called the 'lantern'.
facts.quote: The structure has three main components: an L-shaped office building, a 21-story high glass-enclosed atrium, and a hanging structure referred to as the 'lantern.'

facts.fact: The south and west walls shade out direct summer sun with a travertine fin-wall and brise soleil shades that keep the views.
facts.quote: The south and west walls of the building deflect direct summer sun with a travertine fin-wall and brise soleil shades that don't obstruct views.

facts.fact: Its glass cable-net wall, 90 metres high and 60 metres wide, is the world's largest.

facts.fact: The wall is counterweighted by an eight-storey lantern hanging from four parallel strand cables.
facts.quote: The wall is counterweighted with an 8-story "lantern" structure hanging from four parallel strand cables.

facts.quote: The lantern structure, essentially a building hanging from another building, has no support columns at the ground.

facts.fact: The lantern houses the Poly Museum, named for its likeness to a pleated Chinese lantern.
facts.quote: It is referred to as the lantern for its resemblance to a pleated Chinese lantern.

facts.fact: The six-floor neo-classical building on the Bund was the Shanghai headquarters of HSBC from 1923 to 1955.

facts.fact: It was designed by the British firm Palmer & Turner and built from 5 May 1921 to 23 June 1923.
facts.quote: Designed by the British architecture firm Palmer & Turner architects and surveyors, construction of the building lasted from 5 May 1921 to 23 June 1923.

facts.fact: The exterior is strictly neo-classical, divided in three both vertically and horizontally.

facts.fact: A central dome rises over six Ionic columns that run from the second to the fourth storey.

facts.fact: The structure is a steel lattice filled with brick, faced in granite.

facts.fact: The main trading hall has four columns hewn from whole blocks of marble, then unique in Asia.
facts.quote: The main trading hall has four columns hewn from whole blocks of marble, which was at the time unique in Asia.

facts.fact: The building's mosaics were rediscovered and uncovered during renovations in 1997.
facts.quote: In 1997, the mosaics were rediscovered, renovations uncovered them.

facts.fact: The museum is housed in the former Royal Asiatic Society building on Huqiu Road near the Bund, completed in 1933.
facts.quote: The museum is on Huqiu Road, in the former Royal Asiatic Society building completed in 1933 near The Bund waterfront.

facts.fact: Begun in 1932, the five-storey Art Deco building held a lecture hall, a library and a museum.

facts.fact: The building was originally designed by the British firm Palmer and Turner.

facts.fact: Chipperfield kept the main facade faithful to the original 1932 design.

facts.fact: The biggest change is a skylight joining the upper three floors.

facts.fact: The museum has no permanent collection.

facts.quote: The Hainan Science and Technology Museum (Chinese: 海南科技馆) is located in Haikou's west coast area, Hainan, China. It was completed in 2025.

facts.fact: The silver building has a spiral design around a large open core.

facts.fact: Its exterior is covered with 843 fibre-reinforced polymer panels.

facts.fact: It is held up by three concrete core tubes.

facts.fact: It was designed by Ma Yansong and others at MAD Architects.
facts.quote: The building was designed by Ma Yansong and others at his company MAD Architects.

facts.fact: Inside are a planetarium and a large-screen cinema; the building covers 45,528 square metres.

facts.fact: The grounds have a covered plaza and a reflecting pool.

facts.quote: The Red House was listed as a Class III Historical Site in 1997.

facts.quote: It is one of the two main concert venues in Shenzhen, the other being Nanshan cultural center (南山文体中心剧院).

facts.fact: The Belt and Road International Music Festival was inaugurated at the concert hall in 2019.
facts.quote: The Belt and Road International Music Festival was inaugurated at Shenzhen concert hall in 2019.

facts.fact: Construction began in 2011, three years after the 2008 Olympics, and it was completed in 2014.
facts.quote: Construction began in 2011, three years after the 2008 Summer Olympics; it was completed in 2014, and opened on August 8, 2015.

facts.fact: It is used only for observation, with no offices or apartments.
facts.quote: It is used strictly for observation; there is no provision for offices or apartments.

facts.fact: The winning competition design was by Cui Kai and Li Cundong of the China Architecture Design and Research Group; Zhao Wenbin designed the landscaping at the base.
facts.quote: The winning design was by Cui Kai and Li Cundong of the Chinese Architecture Design and Research Group (CARDEG). Zhao Wenbin, another architect at the firm, designed the landscaping at the towers' base.

facts.fact: At 258 metres it is the second tallest tower in Beijing.
facts.quote: At 258 metres (846 ft) in height it is the second tallest tower in the city after the Central Radio & TV Tower, and the fourth-tallest structure in the city.

facts.fact: Four smaller circular floors at different heights below a larger top are meant to echo the Olympic rings; the design was inspired by blades of grass.
facts.quote: Its design, with four smaller circular floors at different heights and positions below a larger top floor, is meant to echo the Olympic rings. The overall design was inspired by blades of grass; however it has also been likened to "huge nails".

facts.fact: Five circular steel towers rise from one concrete foundation, the tallest surrounded by the other four.
facts.quote: A slight landscaped rise surrounds their base, from which all five circular steel towers rise. The largest and tallest, 258 metres (846 ft) in total height, is surrounded by the other four.

facts.fact: Large diagonal members tie the lesser towers to the main one, and all widen at their tops into observation platforms.
facts.quote: Large diagonal members connect the lesser towers to the main structure. All the towers widen at their flat-roofed tops to allow the use of the space inside as observation platforms.

facts.fact: The steel exterior opens into latticework to allow views from the glass behind.
facts.quote: The solid steel exterior parts into latticework to allow views from the glass behind them.

facts.fact: Shanghai Library East, a branch of the main library in Pudong, opened in 2022.
facts.quote: Shanghai Library East, a branch of the main library located in Pudong, opened in 2022.

facts.fact: Schmidt Hammer Lassen designed it with local artists, as an abstract reference to the taihu stones that inspired Jin dynasty scholars.
facts.quote: The architectural firm Schmidt Hammer Lassen was selected to construct the building in consultation with local artists, who designed it with abstract reference to the taihu stones used for inspiration by Jin dynasty scholars.

facts.fact: It won several local and national awards and was among the winners of the 2026 RIBA International Award for Excellence.
facts.quote: The building won several local and national awards, and was among the winners of the 2026 RIBA International Award for Excellence.

facts.fact: Unlike the main building, it has an open plan that gives most of its space to the local community, while holding 4.8 million books.
facts.quote: The East branch departs from the main building by having an open plan that makes the majority of its space available for the local community to use, while still containing 4.8 million books.

facts.fact: It is one of China's largest new libraries and opened in September 2022.
facts.quote: Notable projects include the national library of Denmark The Royal Library (Det Kgl. Bibliotek) in Copenhagen, the ARoS Kunstmuseum in Aarhus, DOKK1, the largest public library in Scandinavia and named by IFLA International Federation of Library Associations as Public Library of the Year in 2016, and Shanghai Library East, one of China's largest new library's which opened in September 2022.

facts.fact: Schmidt Hammer Lassen is an architecture firm founded by Danish architects in Aarhus in 1986, with an office in Shanghai.
facts.quote: Schmidt Hammer Lassen (SHL) is an international architectural firm founded by a group of Danish architects in 1986 in Aarhus, Denmark. It has offices in Copenhagen and Aarhus in Denmark, and Shanghai, China.

facts.fact: Completed in 1987, the two buildings stand on the south and north sides of Liberty Square, with Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall to the east.
facts.quote: Completed in 1987, the landmarks stand on the south and north sides of the square with Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall to the east.

facts.fact: They were among the first major modern performing arts buildings in Asia.
facts.quote: The National Theater and National Concert Hall are two of the first major modern performing arts facilities to be established in Asia.

facts.fact: Yang Cho-cheng and Architects and Engineers Associates did the overall design.
facts.quote: Yang Cho-cheng and Architects and Engineers Associates were responsible for the overall design.

facts.fact: Though modern in function, the buildings recall traditional Chinese palace architecture.
facts.quote: The buildings, though modern in function and purpose, recall traditional elements of Chinese palace architecture.

facts.fact: Germany's G+H and the Dutch firm Philips led the design of the interiors, stage lighting and acoustics.
facts.quote: The G+H Company of Germany and Philips, based in The Netherlands, played leading roles in the design of the interior facilities, stage lighting and acoustics.

facts.fact: The Flentrop organ in the Concert Hall was the largest in Asia when installed in 1987.
facts.quote: The pipe organ by Flentrop Orgelbouw in the National Concert Hall was the largest organ in Asia at the time of its installation in 1987.

facts.fact: The Concert Hall seats 2,022, with a 354-seat Recital Hall.
facts.quote: The main hall is the Concert Hall (2022 seats); the smaller is the Recital Hall (354 seats).

facts.fact: The Theater's main proscenium house seats 1,498, beside a flexible black-box Experimental Theater.
facts.quote: The main theater is Proscenium Arch Theater (1498 seats); the smaller Experimental Theater is a flexible "Black Box Theater".

facts.fact: Sullivan Center, formerly the Carson Pirie Scott store, is a 12-storey building at State and Madison streets in Chicago.
facts.quote: Sullivan Center (formerly known as the Schlesinger & Mayer Building, Carson Pirie Scott Building, or Carson, Pirie, Scott and Company Store) is a 12-story building at State and Madison streets in Chicago, Illinois, United States.

facts.fact: Opened in phases from 1899 to 1907, it was designed by Louis Sullivan for Schlesinger & Mayer and was his last large commercial building.
facts.quote: Opened in phases between 1899 and 1907, the building was designed by Louis Sullivan, originally for retail firm Schlesinger & Mayer, and was Sullivan's last large commercial building.

facts.fact: It is a Chicago Landmark and a National Historic Landmark.
facts.quote: The building is a Chicago Landmark and National Historic Landmark and is part of the Loop Retail Historic District.

facts.fact: The two street facades meet at a curved corner, and piers divide them into bays of wide Chicago windows.
facts.quote: The main elevations of the building's facade on State and Madison streets, are connected by a curved corner. On each elevation, piers divide the facade into bays with wide Chicago windows.

facts.fact: The lowest two storeys are clad in decorative cast iron, with the entrance at the corner.
facts.quote: The lowest two stories are clad with decorative cast iron, with an entrance at the corner and large windows on either elevation.

facts.fact: White terracotta bands frame the windows of the upper storeys.
facts.quote: The windows on the upper stories are framed by white terracotta bands.

facts.fact: Cast iron and steel columns carry terracotta floor slabs, leaving open selling floors between the columns.
facts.quote: The foundation includes a mixture of caissons and pilings, while the superstructure consists of cast iron and steel columns, which support terracotta floor slabs. The store's interior layout was arranged to maximize selling space, with open plan spaces between the columns.

facts.fact: Later additions were made by D. H. Burnham & Company in 1906–1907 and Holabird & Root in 1961.
facts.quote: Subsequent additions were completed by D. H. Burnham & Company in 1906–1907 and Holabird & Root in 1961.

facts.fact: Willis Tower, long called the Sears Tower, is a 110-storey, 442-metre skyscraper in Chicago's Loop.
facts.quote: The Willis Tower, formerly known and still commonly referred to as the Sears Tower, is a 110-story, 1,451-foot (442.3 m) skyscraper in the Loop of Chicago, Illinois, United States.

facts.fact: Designed by architect Bruce Graham and engineer Fazlur Rahman Khan of SOM, it opened in 1973 as the world's tallest building and held the title for nearly 25 years.
facts.quote: Designed by architect Bruce Graham and engineer Fazlur Rahman Khan of Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM), it opened in 1973 as the world's tallest building, a title that it held for nearly 25 years.

facts.fact: Graham and Khan designed it as nine square tubes in a 3×3 grid, seven of which step back higher up.
facts.quote: Graham and Khan designed the building as nine square "tubes", clustered in a 3×3 matrix; seven of the tubes set back at upper floors.

facts.fact: The facade is anodised aluminium and black glass.
facts.quote: The facade is made of anodized aluminum and black glass.

facts.fact: Each tube is a column-free module 75 by 75 feet, with setbacks at the 50th, 66th and 90th floors.
facts.quote: Each of the "tubes" is a column-free module measuring 75 by 75 feet (23 by 23 m), which set back at different stories. There are setbacks at the 50th, 66th, and 90th floors.

facts.fact: The setbacks gave Sears its large lower floors while offering more ordinary office floors to rent higher up.
facts.quote: This allowed Sears to occupy the large lower stories, while providing more conventional office space that could be rented out on the upper stories.

facts.fact: Its Skydeck, the highest observation deck in the United States, draws more than 1.7 million visitors a year.
facts.quote: Each year, more than 1.7 million people visit the Skydeck, the highest observation deck in the United States, making it one of Chicago's most popular tourist destinations.

facts.fact: It remains the tallest building in Chicago.
facts.quote: It currently remains the tallest building in Chicago, the third-tallest building in the Western Hemisphere, as well as the 26th-tallest in the world.

facts.fact: The Minneapolis Central Library is the public library in downtown Minneapolis and the largest in the Hennepin County Library system.
facts.quote: The Minneapolis Central Library is a public library located in downtown Minneapolis, Minnesota, United States. It is the largest library in the Hennepin County Library system.

facts.fact: The 353,000 sq ft building at 300 Nicollet Mall was designed by César Pelli and opened on 20 May 2006.
facts.quote: The 353,000-square-foot (32,800 m2) building at 300 Nicollet Mall with two levels of underground parking was designed by César Pelli and opened on May 20, 2006.

facts.fact: Pelli designed it with the Minneapolis firm Architectural Alliance.
facts.quote: The new building was designed by César Pelli, along with the Minneapolis firm Architectural Alliance, and opened to the public on May 20, 2006.

facts.fact: It has an 8,140 sq ft atrium and an 18,560 sq ft green roof of low-growing, sun- and drought-resistant ground cover, plus many energy-saving measures.
facts.quote: It has over 300 computers for use by the public, an 8,140-square-foot (756 m2) atrium, an 18,560-square-foot (1,724 m2) green roof planted with low-growing ground cover designed to "be sun- and drought-resistant", and a host of energy-efficiency measures.

facts.fact: The library has a roof garden and plenty of daylight, at a cost of $250 per square foot.
facts.quote: At a cost of $250 per square foot, the library features a roof garden and substantial daylight.

facts.fact: Its storage was designed so the public can reach nearly all of the collection without staff help.
facts.quote: Its storage area was designed to be available to the public without staff assistance so that nearly all of the collection is accessible to the public.

facts.fact: Construction began after Minneapolis voters approved $140 million for library services on 7 November 2000.
facts.quote: Construction on the third and current library began (on the same location as the demolished second building) after Minneapolis voters approved a $140 million in funding to improve library services on November 7, 2000.

facts.fact: Hy-Vee Arena, formerly Kemper Arena, is an indoor arena in Kansas City, Missouri, once a 19,500-seat professional sports arena.
facts.quote: Hy-Vee Arena, previously known as Kemper Arena, is an indoor arena located in Kansas City, Missouri. Prior to conversion to a youth sports and community gymnasium facility, Kemper Arena was previously a 19,500-seat professional sports arena.

facts.fact: It was built in 18 months in 1973–74 on the site of the former Kansas City Stockyards.
facts.quote: Kemper Arena was built in 18 months in 1973–74 on the site of the former Kansas City Stockyards just west of downtown in the West Bottoms to replace the 8,000-seat Municipal Auditorium to play host to the city's professional basketball and hockey teams.

facts.fact: It was the first major project of the German architect Helmut Jahn.
facts.quote: The arena was the first major project of German architect Helmut Jahn, who was to go on to become an important architect of his era.

facts.fact: It had no interior columns blocking views; the roof hangs from exterior steel trusses.
facts.quote: The building was revolutionary in its simplicity and the fact it did not have interior columns obstructing views. Its roof is suspended by exterior steel trusses.

facts.fact: Steel trusses hanging from three huge portals carried the reinforced concrete roof.
facts.quote: Steel trusses that hung from three huge portals supported the reinforced concrete roof.

facts.fact: Its exterior-skeleton approach became a feature of many of Jahn's later projects.
facts.quote: Kemper's exterior skeleton style was to be used extensively throughout Jahn's other projects.

facts.fact: The American Institute of Architects gave it an Honor award in 1976.
facts.quote: The American Institute of Architects had given the building an "Honor" award in 1976, and the AIA, coincidentally, was holding its annual national conference in Kansas City half a mile away at nearby Bartle Hall.

facts.fact: The new roof was welded rather than bolted and fitted with sensors to detect weaknesses in the structure.
facts.quote: The arena's new roof was welded together instead of bolted, and it featured a state-of-the-art network of sensors intended to detect weaknesses in the structure.

facts.fact: It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2016 for Jahn's revolutionary design.
facts.quote: In 2016, it was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in recognition of its revolutionary design by Helmut Jahn.

facts.fact: The Waterwall is a multi-storey sculptural fountain opposite the south face of Williams Tower in Houston's Uptown District.
facts.quote: The Gerald D. Hines Waterwall Park, formerly the Williams Waterwall and the Transco Waterwall, is a multi-story sculptural fountain that sits opposite the south face of Williams Tower in the Uptown District of Houston.

facts.fact: The fountain and the tower were both designed by John Burgee Architects with Philip Johnson.
facts.quote: Both the fountain and tower were designed by John Burgee Architects with Philip Johnson.

facts.fact: The Waterwall was fully operational in 1985.
facts.quote: The Waterwall was fully and regularly operational in 1985.

facts.fact: The semicircular fountain is 64 feet tall, for the tower's 64 storeys, and sits among 118 Texas live oaks.
facts.quote: The semi-circular fountain is 64 feet (20 m) tall, to symbolize the 64 stories of the tower, and sits among 118 Texas live oak trees.

facts.fact: Water falls in sheets from the narrow top rim to the wider base, on both the inner and outer sides.
facts.quote: Water cascades in vast channeled sheets from the narrower top rim of the circle to the wider base below, both on the concave side and on the convex side.

facts.fact: It is built mainly of St. Joe brick, with limestone Romanesque arches and a black granite base.
facts.quote: The main building material of the fountain is St. Joe brick. However, the Romanesque arches are made of Indiana Buss limestone, while the wall's base is black granite.

facts.fact: Its 78,500 gallons of water are recycled every three hours and two minutes.
facts.quote: The entire fountain's water supply, consisting of 78,500 gallons is recycled by an internal mechanism every three hours and two minutes.

facts.fact: The Hall of State in Dallas's Fair Park commemorates the history of Texas and is one of the state's best Art Deco buildings.
facts.quote: The Hall of State (originally the State of Texas Building) is a building in Dallas's Fair Park that commemorates the history of the U.S. state of Texas and is considered one of the best examples of Art Deco architecture in the state.

facts.fact: It was designed and built for the Texas Centennial Exposition.
facts.quote: It was designed and built for the Texas Centennial Exposition.

facts.fact: Donald Barthelme became chief designer in July 1935, and his design was approved that month.
facts.quote: The next day, Mark Lemmon offered Donald Barthelme the position of chief designer for the State of Texas building. By July 9, Barthelme presented his designs, which were approved by the State Board of Control in Austin.

facts.fact: It was dedicated on 6 September 1936 and cost $1.2 million.
facts.quote: The building was officially dedicated as the State of Texas building on September 6, 1936. The building's cost totalled $1.2 million.

facts.fact: The curved entrance exedra has 76-foot limestone pillars in front of blue tiles that evoke the bluebonnet.
facts.quote: The curved exedra at the entrance to the Hall of Texas features 76-foot (23 m) tall limestone pillars sit in front of blue tiles designed to evoke the state's flower, the bluebonnet (Lupinus texensis).

facts.fact: The building is T-shaped, with four rooms for the regions of Texas.
facts.quote: The building is designed in the shape of a T, and has four interior rooms representing regions found in Texas: West, East, North and South.

facts.fact: The Great Hall is 46 feet high, and its columns are reeded Texas limestone.
facts.quote: This main room in the building is forty-six feet high, ninety-four feet long, and sixty-eight feet wide. The columns are reeded Cordova Cream shell stone, a quarried Texas limestone.

facts.fact: It became a Recorded Texas Historic Landmark in 1981.
facts.quote: The building became a Recorded Texas Historic Landmark in 1981.

facts.fact: The Nasher Museum of Art is Duke University's art museum, on its campus in Durham, North Carolina.
facts.quote: The Nasher Museum of Art (previously the Duke University Museum of Art) is the art museum of Duke University, and is located on Duke's campus in Durham, North Carolina, United States.

facts.fact: Helped by a gift from alumnus Raymond Nasher, the museum opened a new $24 million building designed by Rafael Viñoly.
facts.quote: In the early twenty-first century, in part from a gift by alumnus Raymond Nasher, the museum became known as the Nasher Museum of Art and opened a new $24 million museum  designed by architect Rafael Viñoly.

facts.fact: Viñoly's list of works dates the museum to 2005.
facts.quote: Nasher Museum of Art, Duke University, Durham, North Carolina, 2005

facts.fact: Since reopening it has drawn about 100,000 visitors a year.
facts.quote: Since its reopening, annual attendance is about 100,000 visitors.

facts.fact: The museum is dedicated to contemporary art from around the world, with particular attention to historically underrepresented artists.
facts.quote: The museum is dedicated to presenting contemporary art from around the world, with particular attention given to those who have been historically underrepresented.

facts.fact: It holds a strong collection of 3,300 Pre-Columbian objects.
facts.quote: The museum has a strong collection of Pre-Columbian art (3,300 objects), with particularly significant holdings of Mayan ceramics and Peruvian textiles.

facts.fact: The center formally opened on 9 September 2006 with a gala concert conducted by Leonard Slatkin.
facts.quote: The center formally opened on September 9, 2006, with a gala concert conducted by Leonard Slatkin and broadcast by PBS affiliates throughout the state.

facts.fact: David M. Schwarz Architects designed it, with Earl Swensson Associates of Nashville as architect of record.
facts.quote: The firm of the 2015 Driehaus Prize winner, David M. Schwarz Architects, Inc., of Washington, D.C., designed the center, with Earl Swensson Associates of Nashville as architect of record.

facts.fact: Its heart is the 1,844-seat Laura Turner Concert Hall, a shoebox-style hall and home of the Nashville Symphony.
facts.quote: At the heart of Schermerhorn Symphony Center is the 30,000 square feet (2,800 m2), 1,844-seat Laura Turner Concert Hall, which is home to the Nashville Symphony. The hall is of the shoebox style.

facts.fact: Daylight enters through 30 soundproof, double-paned clerestory windows.
facts.quote: It features natural lighting, which streams in through 30 soundproof, double-paned clerestory windows.

facts.fact: The New Classical design draws on other Classical buildings in the city, such as the Parthenon replica.
facts.quote: The center's New Classical design blends elements of other Classical and Neoclassical structures in the city, such as the full-scale Parthenon replica and Nashville's main public library.

facts.fact: Motorised seat wagons sink into the floor so the hall can become a ballroom in about two hours.
facts.quote: These "chair-wagons" enable the concert hall to be converted into a 5,700-square-foot (530 m2) ballroom in approximately two hours.

facts.fact: A 2-inch air gap around the hall, an acoustical isolation joint, keeps outside noise out.
facts.quote: The Laura Turner Concert Hall is insulated from exterior noise by an acoustical isolation joint, a 2-inch gap of air that encircles the hall and prevents transmission of sound waves in or out.

facts.fact: Its Schoenstein & Co. concert organ has 3,568 pipes.
facts.quote: The hall also features the custom-built Martin Foundation Concert Organ, crafted by Schoenstein & Co. of San Francisco, which has 47 voices, 64 ranks, and 3,568 pipes with three 32-foot stops.

facts.fact: The Memphis Pyramid stands on the Mississippi in downtown Memphis and was built in 1991 as a 20,142-seat arena.
facts.quote: The Memphis Pyramid, formerly known as the Great American Pyramid and the Pyramid Arena, and colloquially known as the Bass Pro Shops Pyramid, is a pyramid-shaped building located in downtown Memphis, Tennessee, United States, at the bank of the Mississippi River. Built in 1991 as a 20,142-seat arena, the facility was owned and operated jointly by the city of Memphis and Shelby County until Shelby County sold its share to Memphis in April 2009.

facts.fact: Its form plays on the city's namesake in Egypt, known for its pyramids.
facts.quote: Its structure plays on the city's namesake in Egypt, which is known for its ancient pyramids.

facts.fact: It is 321 feet tall, about 32 storeys, with base sides of 591 feet.
facts.quote: It is 321 feet (98 m) (about 32 stories) tall and has base sides of 591 feet (180 m); it is by some measures the tenth-tallest pyramid in the world.

facts.fact: The idea began around 1954 with the Memphis artist Mark C. Hartz.
facts.quote: The Great American Pyramid was first conceived around 1954 by Mark C. Hartz, a Memphis artist.

facts.fact: Ground was broken on 15 September 1989 and the building opened on 9 November 1991.
facts.quote: The groundbreaking ceremony was held on September 15, 1989, and the building was opened on November 9, 1991.

facts.fact: In 2015 it reopened as a Bass Pro Shops megastore, with an outdoor observation deck by its apex.
facts.quote: In 2015, the Pyramid re-opened as a Bass Pro Shops megastore, which included shopping, a hotel, restaurants, a bowling alley, and an archery range, with an outdoor observation deck adjacent to its apex.

facts.fact: The city spent $30 million on a seismic retrofit, with O.T. Marshall Architects.
facts.quote: The city invested $30 million and hired O.T. Marshall Architects to help with the seismic retrofitting of the structure, which was funded by sales tax revenue in the surrounding area.

facts.fact: A freestanding elevator, the tallest in America, takes visitors to the Lookout at the apex.
facts.quote: The tallest freestanding elevator in America takes visitors to the Lookout at the Pyramid at the apex of the building, where people can take in the view on an indoor and outdoor observation deck or dine and drink at the Lookout, which is a restaurant, bar, and aquarium at the top of the building.

facts.fact: The Capitol Complex was designed jointly by Edward Durell Stone & Associates of New York and Reynolds, Smith & Hills of Jacksonville.
facts.quote: The current Capitol Complex design was a joint venture of the architectural firms of Edward Durell Stone & Associates of New York City and Reynolds, Smith & Hills of Jacksonville.

facts.fact: It is a concrete New Formalist building, with metal louvers shading the windows, meant to symbolise Florida's modern development.
facts.quote: The Capitol is a concrete building designed in the New Formalist style with metal louvers shading the windows. The design symbolized the modern development of Florida.

facts.fact: It is usually counted as 22 storeys and 345 feet tall.
facts.quote: The Capitol is usually referred to as a twenty-two-story building with a height of 345 feet (105 m).

facts.fact: Stone's list of works dates it to 1977, with Reynolds, Smith & Hills as associated architects.
facts.quote: Florida State Capitol, Tallahassee, Florida (Reynolds, Smith & Hills, associated architects, 1977)

facts.fact: Four-storey Senate and House office buildings stand at either end, joined to the Capitol by bridges.
facts.quote: The Senate office building and the House office building are each four stories high and on either end of the Capitol Complex. The bridges on the second and third floors allow people to walk between the Capitol and office buildings.

facts.fact: The observation deck on the 22nd floor is 307 feet above the Plaza Level.
facts.quote: The Observation Deck is the top or twenty-second floor of the Capitol building. The deck is 307 feet (94 m) above the Plaza Level and 512 feet (156 m) above sea level.

facts.fact: The Historic Capitol of 1845, threatened with demolition when the new one was built, was restored to its 1902 look in 1982 and stands directly behind it.
facts.quote: The Historic Capitol, sometimes called "The Old Capitol", built in 1845, was threatened with demolition in the late 1970s when the new capitol building was built. Having been restored to its 1902-version in 1982, the Historic Capitol is directly behind the new Capitol building.

facts.fact: Its architects assumed the Old Capitol would be removed, so the new design does not reflect the old one.
facts.quote: Therefore, the design of the New Capitol in no way reflected the style of the old one.

facts.fact: The Reynolds Building is a 314-foot Art Deco skyscraper in Winston-Salem, North Carolina.
facts.quote: The Reynolds Building is a 314-foot (96 m) Art Deco skyscraper at 51 East 4th Street in Winston-Salem, North Carolina.

facts.fact: It was completed in 1929 and has 21 floors.
facts.quote: It was completed in 1929 and has 21 floors with 313,996 square feet (29,171.2 m2) of space.

facts.fact: It was built for $2.7 million as the R. J. Reynolds Tobacco Company headquarters and won a national architecture award.
facts.quote: When completed for $2.7 million ($36.3 million in 2016 dollars) as the headquarters of R. J. Reynolds Tobacco Company, it was the tallest building between Baltimore, Maryland; Birmingham, Alabama; and the Miami-Dade County Courthouse, and it won a national architecture award.

facts.fact: It is known as a design inspiration for the much larger Empire State Building of 1931.
facts.quote: The building is well known for being a design inspiration for the much larger Empire State Building that was built in 1931 in New York City.

facts.fact: The architects, Shreve & Lamb, were asked for conservatism and attractiveness without flashiness.
facts.quote: Shreve & Lamb, the architects, were asked for "an effect of conservatism along with attractiveness, but to avoid flashiness."

facts.fact: Like the Empire State Building, it was designed for corporate offices with shops on the first floor.
facts.quote: The building was designed, just as the Empire State Building, for the purpose of corporate offices with retail outlets on the first floor.

facts.fact: It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2014.
facts.quote: It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2014.

facts.fact: In 2016 the top 11 floors opened as apartments and the first six as the Kimpton Cardinal Hotel.
facts.quote: In March 2016, The Residences @ the R.J. Reynolds Building, apartments located on the top 11 floors, opened. The first six floors opened as the Kimpton Cardinal Hotel in April.

facts.fact: The First Baptist Church is one of seven National Historic Landmarks in Columbus, Indiana.
facts.quote: The First Baptist Church is one of seven National Historic Landmarks in Columbus, Indiana, United States.

facts.fact: It was designed by Harry Weese and completed in 1965.
facts.quote: It was designed by distinguished architect Harry Weese and completed in 1965.

facts.fact: It was one of the first church designs to combine Modern movement architecture with a non-traditional church plan.
facts.quote: It was one of the first church designs to integrate Modern movement architecture and a non-traditional church plan.

facts.fact: Few alterations have been made since completion.
facts.quote: Since completion, few alterations have been made and the building has retained its integrity.

facts.fact: It sits on a 7.1-acre site at the foot of a gently sloping hill.
facts.quote: The facility occupies a 7.1-acre (2.9 ha) site at the base of a gently sloping hill which the group chose because the site allowed room for growth and parking.

facts.fact: The red brick building has five sections (narthex, sanctuary, office wing, fellowship hall and chapel) around a central courtyard.
facts.quote: The red brick building has five distinct sections (narthex, sanctuary, office wing, fellowship hall, and chapel) built around a central courtyard.

facts.fact: The sanctuary is a windowless room of simple elements that is both dramatic and serene.
facts.quote: It is a windowless room, made up of simple elements that combine to create a space that is at the same time dramatic and serene.

facts.fact: Each element (a brick wall, a beam, an opening, a skylight) is slightly exaggerated in size, proportion or height.
facts.quote: Each element is a simple object—a brick wall, a beam, an opening, a skylight—but all exaggerated slightly in size, proportion, or height.

facts.fact: Robert Venturi's list of works includes Fire Station No. 4 in Columbus, Indiana, of 1968.
facts.quote: Fire Station #4; Columbus, Indiana (1968)

facts.fact: The meeting house was designed by Frank Lloyd Wright, built by Marshall Erdman in 1949–1951, and is a National Historic Landmark.
facts.quote: Its meeting house was designed by Frank Lloyd Wright and built by Marshall Erdman in 1949–1951, and has been designated a National Historic Landmark for its architecture.

facts.fact: Wright was a member of the society and the son of two of its founders.
facts.quote: The society is housed in the historic Unitarian Meeting House, which was designed by Frank Lloyd Wright, one of its members and the son of two of its founders.

facts.fact: Its form has been read as a ship's prow, a plough cutting the prairie, and hands folded in prayer.
facts.quote: The dramatic result has been variously interpreted as the prow of a ship, a plow cutting through the prairie, and hands folded in prayer.

facts.fact: To cut costs, members of the congregation hauled limestone blocks for the walls.
facts.quote: To cut the cost, members of the congregation hauled limestone blocks for the walls.

facts.fact: The prow-like roof is covered in blue-green standing-seam copper.
facts.quote: The church's "upper meeting house", the original Wright design, is characterized by its prow-like roof, covered with a blue-green standing seam copper, set with a combination of vertical and horizontal seams to emphasize the roof's shape.

facts.fact: Hinged-arch trusses of two-by-four and two-by-six timber carry the roof.
facts.quote: The roof is supported by an innovative series of hinged-arch trusses built out of two-by-four and two-by-six framing members.

facts.fact: The system gives an interior span of 64 feet without supports.
facts.quote: The system allows for an interior span of 64 feet (20 m) without supports.

facts.fact: Wright designed it around triangles, writing that the triangle stands for aspiration.
facts.quote: Wright designed the structure around triangles, and after it was built he wrote: "As the square has always signified integrity and the sphere universality, the triangle stands for aspiration. Here is a church where the whole edifice is in the attitude of prayer."

facts.fact: UTS Building 1, the UTS Tower, is a landmark on Broadway at the southern gateway to Sydney's central business district.
facts.quote: UTS Building 1, also known as the UTS Tower, is a landmark building on Broadway at the southern gateway to Sydney's central business district.

facts.fact: Many of the University of Technology Sydney's administrative units occupy its 27 floors.
facts.quote: Many of the administrative units of the University of Technology, Sydney are located across the building's 27 occupied floors.

facts.fact: It was completed in 1979 in the brutalist style from a 1968 plan by Michael Dysart of the NSW Government Architect's Office.
facts.quote: Completed in 1979 in the brutalist architectural style from a 1968 plan by Michael Dysart of the NSW Government Architect's Office, the Tower was officially opened by NSW Premier Neville Wran.

facts.fact: The original 1964 plan had three towers plus a podium, but funding cuts in the 1970s reduced it to the main tower and an 11-level Building 2.
facts.quote: The original 1964 plan envisaged three towers of varying heights plus a podium. By the mid-1970s, with cutbacks in commonwealth funding, the original plan was reduced to the main Tower and smaller 11-level Building 2 next door.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1969, and at its opening on 15 October 1979 it was declared Australia's tallest educational building.
facts.quote: Construction of the building commenced in 1969 and lower floors were occupied from 1975. The building was officially opened on 15 October 1979 by the NSW Premier Neville Wran where the Tower was declared the tallest educational facility in Australia at the time.

facts.fact: It has often been called Sydney's ugliest building, including by Frank Gehry.
facts.quote: The Tower has been described very colourfully and identified numerous times as Sydney's ugliest building, notably in The Sydney Morning Herald, and by architect Frank Gehry.

facts.fact: Its place on the skyline has also been seen positively, as marking Sydney as a university town.
facts.quote: The Tower's visibility in the central business district skyline has also been described positively, as marking Sydney as a University town.

facts.fact: UTS Central, opened in 2019 beside it, connects to the Tower across four levels.
facts.quote: UTS Central (Building 2) opened in August 2019 and features direct pedestrian connections with the UTS Tower across four levels.

facts.fact: The Sydney Harbour Bridge is a steel through-arch bridge spanning Sydney Harbour from the CBD to the North Shore.
facts.quote: The Sydney Harbour Bridge is a steel through arch bridge in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia, spanning Sydney Harbour from the central business district (CBD) to the North Shore.

facts.fact: Nicknamed "the Coathanger", it carries rail, road, bicycle and pedestrian traffic.
facts.quote: Nicknamed "the Coathanger" because of its arch-based design, the bridge carries rail, vehicular, bicycle and pedestrian traffic.

facts.fact: Under the direction of John Bradfield, it was designed and built by Dorman Long of Middlesbrough and opened in 1932.
facts.quote: Under the direction of John Bradfield of the New South Wales Department of Public Works, the bridge was designed and built by British firm Dorman Long of Middlesbrough, and opened in 1932.

facts.fact: The chosen design was Dorman Long's own, drawing partly on its Tyne Bridge.
facts.quote: The design chosen from the tender responses was original work created by Dorman Long, who leveraged some of the design from its own Tyne Bridge.

facts.fact: The arch spans 504 metres, with its summit 134 metres above sea level.
facts.quote: The arch has a span of 504 m (1,654 ft), and its summit is 134 m (440 ft) above mean sea level; expansion of the steel structure on hot days can increase the height of the arch by 18 cm (7.1 in).

facts.fact: It is held together by six million hand-driven rivets.
facts.quote: The bridge is held together by six million Australian-made hand-driven rivets supplied by the McPherson company of Melbourne, the last being driven through the deck on 21 January 1932.

facts.fact: At each end stands a pair of 89-metre granite-faced concrete pylons, designed by the Scottish architect Thomas S. Tait.
facts.quote: At each end of the arch stands a pair of 89-metre-high (292 ft) concrete pylons, faced with granite. The pylons were designed by the Scottish architect Thomas S. Tait, a partner in the architectural firm John Burnet & Partners.

facts.fact: The pylons have no structural purpose; they frame the arch and give the bridge better visual balance.
facts.quote: Abutments at the base of the pylons are essential to support the loads from the arch and hold its span firmly in place, but the pylons themselves have no structural purpose. They were included to provide a frame for the arch panels and to give better visual balance to the bridge.

facts.fact: The Public Transport Centre, formerly the Westrail Centre, is a terminal and administration building for public transport in Perth.
facts.quote: The Public Transport Centre (formerly known as the Westrail Centre) is a terminal and administration building for public transport in Perth, Western Australia.

facts.fact: It is the centrepiece of East Perth Terminal, a standard gauge railway station and coach terminal.
facts.quote: It is the centrepiece of East Perth Terminal (formerly known as Perth Terminal), a standard gauge railway station and coach terminal adjacent to East Perth station on the Transperth narrow gauge suburban rail network.

facts.fact: The site was formerly the East Perth Locomotive Depot.
facts.quote: The site occupied by East Perth station, East Perth Terminal, and the Public Transport Centre was formerly the East Perth Locomotive Depot.

facts.fact: The building, above and beside the terminal platform, was commissioned by the Western Australian Government Railways.
facts.quote: The construction of building above and adjacent to the Railway Terminal platform was commissioned by the Western Australian Government Railways (WAGR).

facts.fact: Premier Charles Court opened it as the Westrail Centre on 12 November 1976.
facts.quote: It was opened by State Premier Charles Court on 12 November 1976 as the Westrail Centre.

facts.fact: It is now used by the Public Transport Authority and the Department of Transport.
facts.quote: In 2002, ARG relocated to Welshpool, and the building is now occupied by the Public Transport Authority and Department of Transport having been renamed the Public Transport Centre.

facts.fact: Telstra Tower, also called Black Mountain Tower, is a telecommunications tower and lookout above the summit of Black Mountain in Canberra.
facts.quote: Telstra Tower (also known as Black Mountain Tower and formerly Telecom Tower) is a telecommunications tower and lookout that is situated above the summit of Black Mountain in Australia's capital city of Canberra.

facts.fact: Rising 195.2 metres above the summit, it is the tallest structure in Canberra.
facts.quote: Rising 195.2 metres (640 ft) above the mountain summit, it is the tallest structure in Canberra and a landmark of the city.

facts.fact: It offers panoramic views from an indoor observation deck and two outdoor platforms.
facts.quote: The tower offers panoramic views of Canberra and its surrounding countryside from an indoor observation deck and two outdoor viewing platforms.

facts.fact: The Department of Housing and Construction was responsible for its design.
facts.quote: Design of the tower was the responsibility of the Department of Housing and Construction, however a conflict arose with the National Capital Development Commission which, at the time, had complete control over planning within the Australian Capital Territory.

facts.fact: It drew protests on aesthetic and ecological grounds, as it would sit above Black Mountain in a nature reserve.
facts.quote: During the approval process of the tower, protests arose on aesthetic and ecological grounds. Some people felt that the tower would dominate other aesthetic Canberra structures due to its location above Black Mountain and within a nature reserve.

facts.fact: Prime Minister Malcolm Fraser opened it on 15 May 1980.
facts.quote: Black Mountain Tower was opened on 15 May 1980 by Prime Minister Malcolm Fraser.

facts.fact: Its revolving restaurant turned once every 81 minutes; it closed in 2013.
facts.quote: Former facilities included Canberra's only revolving restaurant which completed a full rotation every 81 minutes, allowing diners to experience a changing view throughout their meal. The restaurant was closed in 2013.

facts.fact: In 1989 it was invited into the World Federation of Great Towers.
facts.quote: In 1989 the World Federation of Great Towers invited the tower to join such distinguished monuments as the CN Tower in Toronto, Blackpool Tower in England and the Empire State Building in New York City.

facts.fact: The Puaka–James Hight Building is the main library building of the University of Canterbury.
facts.quote: The Puaka–James Hight Building is the main library building of the University of Canterbury, and houses the university's Central Library (Māori: Te Puna Mātauraka).

facts.fact: It is 53 metres tall, and its brutalist exposed-concrete design has become the university's most recognisable building.
facts.quote: Rising 53-metres-tall, its distinctive brutalist design, characterised by exposed concrete, confronts the skyline and has become an enduring symbol of the institution, and the most recognisable building on campus.

facts.fact: In 1963 the Ministry of Works was appointed architect for the first phase of the university's complex at Ilam.
facts.quote: In 1963, the University Newsletter announced the appointment of the Ministry of Works as the architect for the initial phase of a comprehensive building complex at Ilam, encompassing the Arts, Library, Administration, and General facilities.

facts.fact: The name Puaka was added to reflect the university's relationship with Ngāi Tahu.
facts.quote: Originally named the James Hight Building, the structure underwent a naming change with the inclusion of "Puaka" to reflect the university's relationship with the mana whenua, Ngāi Tahu.

facts.fact: It was opened on 23 March 1974 and hailed as New Zealand's largest university building.
facts.quote: On 23 March 1974, Governor-General Sir Denis Blundell officially opened the James Hight Library and arts block, heralded as New Zealand's largest university building.

facts.fact: In 1975 the library took the bottom four levels, with academic departments in the tower above.
facts.quote: In 1975, the University Library occupied the bottom four levels of the building, while the Departments of Accountancy, Business Administration, Classics, Economics, Law, Philosophy, and Religious Studies were situated in the tower.

facts.fact: The building was badly damaged in the 2010 and 2011 Christchurch earthquakes.
facts.quote: In the aftermath of the Christchurch earthquakes in 2010 and 2011, the Library suffered substantial damage to the building.

facts.fact: The Manchester Unity Building is an Art Deco Gothic-inspired office and retail building in Melbourne, built in 1931–32 for the Manchester Unity Independent Order of Oddfellows.
facts.quote: The Manchester Unity Building is an Art Deco Gothic inspired office and retail building in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, constructed in 1931–32 for the Manchester Unity Independent Order of Oddfellows.

facts.fact: Its stepped corner tower opposite Melbourne Town Hall makes it one of the city's best-known buildings.
facts.quote: The soaring stepped corner tower on a prominent intersection opposite the Melbourne Town Hall makes it one of the most prominent and best known buildings in Melbourne.

facts.fact: Marcus Barlow designed it; construction began on 1 January 1932 and ran around the clock in eight-hour shifts.
facts.quote: Architect Marcus Barlow designed the building, which was built by W E Cooper Pty Ltd, contracted for the price of £215,000. Construction commenced at midnight on 1 January 1932 with the demolition of the prior buildings on the site, and proceeded around the clock in eight-hour shifts.

facts.fact: It was the first building in Australia managed with a construction progress schedule.
facts.quote: For the first time in Australia a construction progress schedule was used to track and manage the construction of the building:

facts.fact: Barlow's design draws heavily on Raymond Hood's Tribune Tower in Chicago.
facts.quote: Barlow's design clearly draws heavily on the Tribune Tower in Chicago, Illinois.

facts.fact: It is a concrete-encased steel frame clad in 250 tons of terracotta faience tiles.
facts.quote: The building is of concrete-encased steel construction, with the exterior cladding consisting of two hundred and fifty tons of terracotta faience tiles.

facts.fact: The roof is at 132 feet, Melbourne's height limit then, with the ornamental tower and spire rising a further 78 feet.
facts.quote: The building's roof reaches 132 feet (40 m), which was the height limit for buildings in Melbourne at the time of its construction, but the ornamental tower and spire extends a further 78 feet (24 m), as was permitted for non-habitable portions of buildings.

facts.fact: An L-shaped ground-floor arcade links Collins and Swanston streets, richly finished in coloured marble with copper shopfronts.
facts.quote: The ground level included an L shaped arcade connecting Collins to Swanston Street, and into the rear lane, and opening out to form the lift lobby. The arcade is richly finished in coloured marble, with copper shopfronts, and a larger cornice with panels depicting the activities of the society, as well as view of 'old melbourne', and the building itself.

facts.fact: Paganin House is a house in Floreat, Perth, built in 1965.
facts.quote: Paganin House is a residential dwelling in Floreat, a suburb of Perth, Western Australia, built in 1965.

facts.fact: It is one of the best-known buildings by the Bulgarian-born architect Iwan Iwanoff and an iconic example of mid-century modern architecture in Australia.
facts.quote: It is one of the best-known buildings designed by Bulgarian-born architect Iwan Iwanoff and is an iconic example of mid-century modern architecture in Australia.

facts.fact: The Paganin family sold timber and marble, so Iwanoff used both throughout the house, including a marble front verandah.
facts.quote: The Paganin family sold timber and marble, which encouraged extensive use of both materials throughout the house by Iwan Iwanoff, including a notable marble front verandah.

facts.fact: The four-bedroom house has an open, practical layout, called "very expressionistic, very creative, and quite brilliant" by Phil Griffiths of the Australian Institute of Architects.
facts.quote: The four-bedroom home has an open, practical layout, and according to the president of the Western Australian chapter of the Australian Institute of Architects, Phil Griffiths, is "very expressionistic, very creative, and quite brilliant".

facts.fact: It was recommended for the State Heritage Register in 2006.
facts.quote: The house was recommended for listing in the State Heritage Register in 2006 (place number 17607).

facts.fact: WA State Architect Geoff Warn called it a balance of European elegance and the open-plan Case Study Houses of Los Angeles.
facts.quote: In 2015, the home was described by WA State Architect Geoff Warn as "an excellent balance of European elegance and the infamous open-plan Case Study Houses in and around Los Angeles".

facts.fact: The house was restored to Iwanoff's original design and featured on Restoration Australia in 2019.
facts.quote: The house was restored to Iwanoff's original design and featured on Restoration Australia on 17 March 2019.

facts.fact: Built between 1817 and 1819 to house convict men and boys, the brick barracks were designed by the convict architect Francis Greenway.
facts.quote: Originally constructed between 1817 and 1819 as a brick building and compound to house convict men and boys, it was designed by convict architect Francis Greenway.

facts.fact: It is on the UNESCO World Heritage List as one of 11 Australian Convict Sites.
facts.quote: The site is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List as one of 11 pre-eminent Australian Convict Sites as among "the best surviving examples of large-scale convict transportation and the colonial expansion of European powers through the presence and labour of convicts", and was listed on the Australian National Heritage List on 1 August 2007, and on the New South Wales State Heritage Register on 2 April 1999.

facts.fact: Governor Macquarie was so pleased with the design that he gave Greenway a full pardon soon after it was finished.
facts.quote: Macquarie was so impressed by Greenway's design that he granted him a full pardon shortly after its completion.

facts.fact: The main building is a three-storey, gabled Georgian barracks of sandstock brick on sandstone foundations.
facts.quote: The main building is a three-storey sandstock brick, gabled former convict barracks of Georgian style.

facts.fact: The pedimented gable holds an early colonial clock inscribed "L.Macquarie Esq., Governor 1817".
facts.quote: It has sandstone foundations, sills and string courses, while the pedimented gable is decorated by a shaped stone panel containing an early colonial clock. The clock is surmounted by a crown and inscribed "L.Macquarie Esq., Governor 1817".

facts.fact: The facade is divided by brick pilasters, with arched recesses on the ground floor.
facts.quote: The facade is simple but elegant and divided by brick pilasters and arched recesses to the ground floor.

facts.fact: Inside, the four rooms on each floor were hung with two rows of hammocks.
facts.quote: Internally, the four rooms on each floor were hung with two rows of hammocks, with a 0.9-metre (3-foot) passage.

facts.fact: The site closed in January 2019 for an $18 million restoration and reopened in February 2020.
facts.quote: The historic site was closed in January 2019 for $18 million restoration work to transform it into "a rich new, immersive visitor experience like no other in Australia" and reopened in February 2020.

facts.fact: The National Wine Centre of Australia is a public exhibition building about winemaking, opened in 2001.
facts.quote: The National Wine Centre of Australia (commonly the "Wine Centre") is a public exhibition building about winemaking and its industry in South Australia, opened in 2001.

facts.fact: It sits at the eastern end of North Terrace in Adelaide's east parklands, next to the Adelaide Botanic Gardens.
