facts.quote: The main building comprises three storeys, and is of masonry (ground floor) and timber (first and second floors) construction.

facts.fact: The partly sunken ground floor holds a circular assembly hall.
facts.quote: The ground floor is partly subterranean, and houses a circular assembly hall.

facts.fact: Since 1990 it has housed the Suojeluskunta & Lotta Svärd Museum.
facts.quote: Since 1990, the building has been home to the Suojeluskunta & Lotta Svärd Museum, as part of the City of Seinäjoki museum network.

facts.fact: In 2002 the Finnish Heritage Agency protected it as a nationally important built cultural environment.
facts.quote: In 2002, the building complex was designated and protected by the Finnish Heritage Agency as a nationally important built cultural environment (Valtakunnallisesti merkittävä rakennettu kulttuuriympäristö).

facts.fact: The Espoo Cultural Centre in Tapiola, Espoo, is best known for housing Tapiola's central library.
facts.quote: The Espoo Cultural Centre (Finnish: Espoon kulttuurikeskus; Swedish: Esbo kulturcentrum) is a culture centre in Tapiola, Espoo, Finland. It is most famous for hosting the central library of Tapiola.

facts.fact: It also houses the Espoo music academy, the Tapiola Sinfonietta orchestra, the city's cultural office and a folk high school.
facts.quote: The cultural centre houses the Espoo musical academy, the Espoo city orchestra Tapiola Sinfonietta, the Tapiola library, the Espoo city cultural office, the Tapiola general service point, and the Espoo folk high school.

facts.fact: It stands next to the Tapiola Central Tower, between the cultural square and the central pool.
facts.quote: The Espoo cultural centre is located next to the Tapiola Central Tower, between the cultural square and the central pool.

facts.fact: The building was designed by Arto Sipinen and completed in 1989.
facts.quote: The building was designed by the architect Arto Sipinen and was completed in 1989.

facts.fact: It has two halls: Louhisali, 300 seats for theatre, and Tapiolasali, 800 seats for concerts.
facts.quote: The building has two halls: Louhisali, with 300 seats, suitable for theatre, and Tapiolasali, with 800 seats, suitable for concerts.

facts.fact: Arto Sipinen's best-known works include the cultural centres of Espoo, Mikkeli, Imatra and Kuusamo.
facts.quote: Among Sipinen's other best known works are the cultural centres for the cities of Espoo, Mikkeli, Imatra and Kuusamo.

facts.fact: The National Theatre of Iceland in Reykjavík was designed by Guðjón Samúelsson and formally opened on 20 April 1950.
facts.quote: The theater, designed by Guðjón Samúelsson, was formally opened on 20 April 1950.

facts.fact: In downtown Reykjavík, it now performs in five venues, the largest being the 500-seat Main Stage.
facts.quote: The NTI is situated in downtown Reykjavík. Today the theatre performs in five separate venues: the Main Stage (Stóra sviðið; 500 seats), the Black Box (Kassinn; 130 seats), the small stage for children (Kúlan; 80 seats), the experimental space the attic (Loftið; 70 seats) and the theatre cellar cabaret club (Leikhúskjallarinn; 100-120 seats).

facts.fact: Guðjón Samúelsson was State Architect of Iceland and the first Icelander educated in architecture.
facts.quote: Guðjón Samúelsson (16 April 1887 – 25 April 1950) was a State Architect of Iceland, and the first Icelander to be educated in architecture.

facts.fact: As State Architect he tried to create an Icelandic style of architecture.
facts.quote: He tried to create an Icelandic style of architecture.

facts.fact: Westminster Cathedral is the largest Catholic church in England and Wales and the seat of the Archbishop of Westminster.
facts.quote: The Metropolitan Cathedral of the Most Precious Blood of Our Lord Jesus Christ, informally known as Westminster Cathedral, is the largest Catholic church in England and Wales. It is dedicated to the Blood of Jesus Christ, is the seat of the Archbishop of Westminster and the mother church of the Archdiocese of Westminster.

facts.fact: John Francis Bentley designed it in a neo-Byzantine style, built almost entirely of brick without steel; John Betjeman called it 'a masterpiece in striped brick and stone'.
facts.quote: Designed by John Francis Bentley in a 9th-century Christian neo-Byzantine style, and accordingly made almost entirely of brick, without steel reinforcements, Sir John Betjeman called it "a masterpiece in striped brick and stone" that shows "the good craftsman has no need of steel or concrete."

facts.fact: The cathedral opened in 1903, a year after Bentley's death.
facts.quote: The cathedral later opened in 1903, a year after Bentley's death.

facts.fact: The plan is dominated by a wide, uninterrupted nave, 18 m wide and 70 m long, covered with domical vaulting.
facts.quote: The whole building, in the neo-Byzantine style, covers a floor area of about 5,017 square metres (54,000 sq ft); the dominating factor of the scheme, apart from the campanile, being a spacious and uninterrupted nave, 18 metres (59 ft) wide and 70 metres (230 ft) long from the narthex to the sanctuary steps, covered with domical vaulting.

facts.fact: Like a Gothic cathedral the nave is braced by large narrow buttresses, but here they are kept inside the building.
facts.quote: In planning the nave, a system of supports was adopted not unlike that to be seen in most Gothic cathedrals, where huge, yet narrow, buttresses are projected at intervals, and stiffened by transverse walls, arcading and vaulting. Unlike in a Gothic cathedral, at Westminster they are limited to the interior.

facts.fact: Shallow pendentive domes were chosen to keep weight and thrust to a minimum.
facts.quote: In selecting the pendentive type of dome, of shallow concavity, for the main roofing, weight and pressure have been reduced to a minimum.

facts.fact: Outside, bands of white stone run through the red brickwork.
facts.quote: Throughout the exterior, the lavish introduction of white stone bands in connection with the red brickwork (itself quite common in the immediate area) produces an impression quite foreign to the British eye.

facts.fact: The interior decoration had hardly begun at the consecration, because Byzantine decoration is applied rather than built into the architecture.
facts.quote: The decoration of the interior had hardly been started at the time of consecration, as the decoration in Byzantine churches is applied, rather than integral to the architecture.

facts.fact: The Flatiron Building is a 22-storey, 93.6 m steel-framed triangular building at 175 Fifth Avenue in Manhattan, designed by Daniel Burnham and Frederick P. Dinkelberg and opened in 1902.
facts.quote: The Flatiron Building (originally the Fuller Building) is a 22-story, 307-foot-tall (93.6 m) steel-framed triangular building at 175 Fifth Avenue in the Flatiron District neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City, New York, US. Designed by Daniel Burnham and Frederick P. Dinkelberg, it opened in 1902.

facts.fact: The name 'Flatiron' comes from its triangular shape, which recalls a cast-iron clothes iron.
facts.quote: The name "Flatiron" derives from its triangular shape, which recalls that of a cast-iron clothes iron.

facts.fact: The triangular site comes from Broadway's diagonal line across the Manhattan street grid.
facts.quote: The shape of the site arises from Broadway's diagonal alignment relative to the Manhattan street grid.

facts.fact: It was built as the headquarters of the construction firm Fuller Company; construction went quickly and it opened on 1 October 1902, originally 285 feet tall.
facts.quote: The Flatiron Building was developed as the headquarters of construction firm Fuller Company, which acquired the site from the Newhouse family in May 1901. Construction proceeded rapidly, and the building opened on October 1, 1902; it originally stood 285 feet (87 m) tall.

facts.fact: Its facade is divided vertically into three parts like a classical column: a three-storey limestone base and upper floors clad in glazed terracotta.
facts.quote: The Flatiron Building's facade is divided vertically into three sections, similarly to the components of a classical column. The three-story base is clad with limestone, while the upper stories are clad with glazed terracotta.

facts.fact: Its steel frame, by engineers Purdy and Henderson, was designed to withstand four times the area's maximum wind force.
facts.quote: The building's steel frame, designed by structural engineering firm Purdy and Henderson, was intended to withstand four times the maximum wind force of the аrea.

facts.fact: Locals' doubts about its structural safety earned it the early nickname 'Burnham's Folly'.
facts.quote: In its early days, it was sometimes called "Burnham's Folly" because of locals' skepticism of the building's structural integrity.

facts.fact: It became a New York City landmark in 1966 and a National Historic Landmark in 1989.
facts.quote: The building was designated a New York City landmark in 1966, was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1979, and was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1989.

facts.fact: The Yodokō Guest House in Ashiya is a summer villa built for the sake brewer Tazaemon Yamamura, and the only surviving Frank Lloyd Wright residence in Japan.
facts.quote: The Yodokō Guest House (ヨドコウ迎賓館, Yodokōgeihinkan) is a summer villa in Ashiya, Hyōgo, Japan. It was built for the well-to-do Japanese sake brewer of Sakura-Masamune, head of Tazaemon Yamamura, and is the only surviving Frank Lloyd Wright residence in Japan.

facts.fact: It was designed in 1918 and completed in 1924.
facts.quote: The guest house was designed in 1918, and construction was completed in 1924.

facts.fact: Arata Endo supervised its construction after Wright left Japan.
facts.quote: Endo supervised the completion of the Imperial Hotel after Wright's departure in 1922 and also supervised the construction of the Jiyu Gakuen Girls' School and the Yodokō Guest House.

facts.fact: Set into a hilltop, the house has four levels, yet none is taller than two storeys.
facts.quote: Set into a hilltop in Ashiya, overlooking the Port of Kobe in Hyōgo Prefecture, western Japan, the villa demonstrates Wright's genius for spatial composition: although it has four levels, none is taller than two stories.

facts.fact: Stepping the house into the hill let Wright take in the views of Osaka Bay.
facts.quote: By stepping the house into the hill, Wright took advantage of the extraordinary views of Osaka Bay the site offered.

facts.fact: The exterior recalls Wright's Los Angeles textile block houses, but its decorative blocks are Oya stone, not concrete.
facts.quote: The exterior evokes Wright's Los Angeles textile block houses, but its decorative blocks are of Oya stone, not concrete.

facts.fact: In 1974 it became the first Taishō-period building in Japan named an Important Cultural Property.
facts.quote: It was the first Taishō period building in Japan to be named an Important Cultural Property, in 1974.

facts.fact: Damaged in the 1995 Great Hanshin earthquake, it was repaired and reopened.
facts.quote: The building was damaged due to the Great Hanshin earthquake in 1995, but was subsequently repaired and has been re-opened.

facts.fact: Pettit Memorial Chapel, in Belvidere Cemetery, Illinois, was designed by Frank Lloyd Wright and built in 1907.
facts.quote: Pettit Memorial Chapel or Pettit Chapel was designed by architect Frank Lloyd Wright and constructed in 1907. The Pettit Chapel is located in the Belvidere Cemetery in Belvidere, Illinois, United States, and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

facts.fact: It is an example of Wright's Prairie Style and the only funerary structure he designed that was built in his lifetime.
facts.quote: The Pettit Chapel is an example of Frank Lloyd Wright's famed Prairie Style. It is the only funerary structure designed by Wright to be built in his lifetime.

facts.fact: Emma Pettit commissioned it in 1906 in memory of her husband, Dr William Henry Pettit, and gave it to the cemetery.
facts.quote: The Pettit Memorial Chapel is named in honor of Dr. William Henry Pettit (1850–1899) and was donated to the Belvidere Cemetery Association by his widow Emma Glasner Pettit (1855–1924) who commissioned Frank Lloyd Wright to design the structure in 1906, seven years after the death of her husband.

facts.fact: The plan is a T, about 17 by 13 m: the meeting room forms the stem and two open porches the cross bar.
facts.quote: The building has a T-shaped plan which is about 57 ft (17.37 m) by 42 ft (12.8 m), with the meeting room forms the stem of the T and the two open porches form the cross bar.

facts.fact: Wright meant the porch for mourners waiting for their cars after funerals.
facts.quote: Wright meant for the porch to be used by those attending funerals while they waited for cars.

facts.fact: The low-pitched hipped roof keeps the skyline quiet and unbroken, as in Wright's early Prairie houses.
facts.quote: The low-pitched hipped roof presents the skyline as quiet and unbroken, a feature typical of some of Wright's important early Prairie buildings such as the Heurtley House, and the Winslow House.

facts.fact: It shows the essentials of Wright's Prairie style: overhanging eaves, geometric art glass, a raised floor and stucco with contrasting wood trim.
facts.quote: It embodies the very essence of Frank Lloyd Wright's Prairie style buildings: the roof and its overhanging eaves, the abstract geometric art glass windows, the raised functional floor and the "plastic expression" of the stucco exterior and its contrasting wood trim.

facts.fact: It was added to the National Register of Historic Places on 1 December 1978.
facts.quote: The Pettit Memorial Chapel was added to the U.S. National Register of Historic Places on December 1, 1978, Although the National Register nomination discusses Wright's work in relation to several significant monuments designed by Louis H. Sullivan, the Pettit Chapel is not a tomb or mausoleum but a functional building.

facts.fact: The Itatiaia Building is an apartment building in the Centro district of Campinas, Brazil.
facts.quote: The Itatiaia Building (Portuguese: Edifício Itatiaia) is an apartment building in the Centro district of Campinas, São Paulo, Brazil.

facts.fact: Oscar Niemeyer designed it in 1953 and it was completed in 1957.
facts.quote: It was designed by the architect Oscar Niemeyer (1907-2012) in 1953 and completed in 1957.

facts.fact: It was the first Modernist building in Campinas and the city's only residential tower until the early 1960s.
facts.quote: It was the only residential tower in Campinas until the early 1960s, and was the first Modernist building in the city.

facts.fact: It occupies 1,569.8 m² on a trapezoid-shaped plot on Irmã Serafina Avenue.
facts.quote: It occupies 1,569.8 square metres (16,897 ft2) on a trapezoid-shaped plot of land on Irmã Serafina Avenue.

facts.fact: It is often compared with the Copan Building in São Paulo, from the same period.
facts.quote: It is often compared to another of building of the period, the Copan Building (Edifício Copan) in São Paulo.

facts.fact: One Charles Center is a 23-storey aluminium and glass International Style office tower in Baltimore, designed by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe and built in 1962.
facts.quote: It is a 23-story aluminium and glass International Style skyscraper designed by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe and constructed in 1962.

facts.fact: It was Baltimore's first modernist office tower and part of the city's downtown urban renewal.
facts.quote: It was the first modernistic office tower in Baltimore and part of the city's downtown urban renewal movement.

facts.fact: A concrete-faced podium topped by a paved plaza carries the T-shaped tower, trimmed in metal with grey glass.
facts.quote: The base consists of a concrete-faced podium topped by a paved plaza, with the T-shaped office tower atop. The tower includes metal trim and gray glass.

facts.fact: The design followed a competition, and the tower was completed in 13 months for $10,350,000.
facts.quote: The tower was previously the subject of a design competition. It was completed in 13 months at a cost of $10,350,000.

facts.fact: It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2000.
facts.quote: One Charles Center was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2000.

facts.fact: It stands next to the Fidelity Building of the 1890s.
facts.quote: It is located next to the Fidelity Building, which was completed in the 1890s.

facts.fact: It heralded the beginning of Baltimore's modern downtown buildings.
facts.quote: The One Charles Center, built in 1962, is a 23-story aluminum and glass building that heralded the beginning of Baltimore's downtown modern buildings.

facts.fact: Złota 44 is a 192-metre, 52-storey residential skyscraper in central Warsaw, designed by Daniel Libeskind with the Polish architects Artchitecture.
facts.quote: Złota 44 is a residential skyscraper (192 meters high, 52 stories) in central Warsaw, Poland. It was designed by Polish-American architect Daniel Libeskind, in association with Polish architects Artchitecture.

facts.fact: It is sometimes called Żagiel ('sail'), but Libeskind drew on the shape of an eagle's wing, symbolising a changing Warsaw, Poland and freedom.
facts.quote: The building is sometimes referred to as Żagiel (meaning "sail" in Polish) although the skyscraper's architect drew inspiration for Złota 44 from the shape of an eagle's wing symbolizing changing Warsaw, Poland and freedom.

facts.fact: Its name comes from its address on Złota ('Golden') Street.
facts.quote: The building's name comes from its address on Złota ("Golden") Street.

facts.fact: It stands beside Varso Tower, the Palace of Culture and Science and the Złote Tarasy shopping centre.
facts.quote: Złota 44 is located next to Varso Tower, the tallest building in the European Union (310 m), the Palace of Culture and Science, the second tallest building in Poland (237 m), and the Złote Tarasy shopping center.

facts.fact: At 192 metres it is one of the tallest residential buildings in Poland and the European Union, with 287 apartments.
facts.quote: At 192 meters, Złota 44 is one of the tallest residential buildings in Poland and the European Union. The luxury 52-story skyscraper contains 287 apartments.

facts.fact: The apartments are on floors 9 to 52.
facts.quote: The apartments are located between the 9th and 52nd floors.

facts.fact: Construction stopped in 2009 over financial and permit problems, resumed in January 2011, and the building was topped out on 3 February 2012.
facts.quote: Due to financial problems experienced by the developer, as well as invalidation of the construction permit and disputes with the inhabitants of the surrounding buildings, Złota 44's construction was put on hold in 2009, but resumed in January 2011. On 3 February 2012, the building was topped out.

facts.fact: Saint-Denis–Pleyel is a Paris Metro station in Saint-Denis, built for the Grand Paris Express and opened on 24 June 2024 as the terminus of Line 14.
facts.quote: Saint-Denis–Pleyel (French pronunciation: [sɛ̃ dəni plɛjɛl]) is a Paris Metro station located in Saint-Denis, in the northern suburbs of Paris. Built as part of the Grand Paris Express project, the station was opened on 24 June 2024 as the terminus of Line 14.

facts.fact: It will also serve the orbital Line 15 and be the terminus of lines 16 and 17.
facts.quote: In the future, the station will serve the orbital Line 15 and be the terminus of lines 16 and 17.

facts.fact: Kengo Kuma designed it after winning an international architectural competition.
facts.quote: The station was designed by Japanese architect Kengo Kuma, who was selected following an international architectural competition.

facts.fact: Built over nine levels, it will handle 250,000 passengers a day, comparable to Châtelet–Les Halles; its platforms lie 27 m below ground.
facts.quote: Built over 9 levels, the station will be able to accommodate 250,000 passengers a day – comparable to Châtelet–Les Halles. Its platforms are located 27m below ground.

facts.fact: The six tracks of the four lines share one level, with cross-platform changes between lines.
facts.quote: The six tracks of Lines 14, 15, 16 and 17 will be on the same level, with a cross-platform interchange between lines 14 and 15, and between Line 15 and the shared track of lines 16/17.

facts.fact: A new bridge over the Paris–Lille railway links it to the RER D station and the Stade de France.
facts.quote: A new bridge over the Paris-Lille railway lines connects the station to Stade de France–Saint-Denis station on RER D, as well as to the nearby Stade de France.

facts.fact: The station has 56 escalators and 17 lifts.
facts.quote: The station has 56 escalators and 17 elevators.

facts.fact: Torre Realia BCN is a skyscraper on Plaça d'Europa in L'Hospitalet de Llobregat, near Barcelona, paired with the Hotel Porta Fira.
facts.quote: Torre Realia BCN (also Torres de Toyo Ito with Hotel Porta Fira) is a skyscraper on the Plaça d'Europa in the district of Granvia l'Hospitalet in L'Hospitalet de Llobregat, a city of Barcelonès, Catalonia, Spain.

facts.fact: Completed in 2009, it has 24 floors and rises 112 metres.
facts.quote: Completed in 2009, it has 24 floors and rises 112 meters.

facts.fact: Toyo Ito's works list Torre Realia BCN and the Hotel Porta Fira, both of 2009.
facts.quote: 2009 – Torre Realia BCN and Hotel Porta Fira, L'Hospitalet de Llobregat, Barcelona, Spain

facts.fact: Onomichi City Museum of Art opened in Senkō-ji Park in Onomichi, Hiroshima Prefecture, in 1980, and reopened to a design by Tadao Ando in 2003.
facts.quote: Onomichi City Museum of Art (尾道市立美術館, Onomichi shiritsu bijutsukan) opened in Senkō-ji Park in Onomichi, Hiroshima Prefecture, Japan, in 1980. The Museum reopened to a design by Tadao Ando in 2003.

facts.fact: It holds works by artists connected to the city, such as Wasaku Kobayashi, and by foreign artists such as Georges Rouault.
facts.quote: The museum contains artworks by artists connected to the city, such as Guilin-in Hirata and Wasaku Kobayashi, as well as artworks by well known foreign artists such as French painter Georges Rouault.

facts.fact: The museum stands in Senkō-ji Park, about 20 minutes' walk from Onomichi station.
facts.quote: The Museum is located in Senkō-ji Park, roughly 20 minutes walk from Onomichi station.
